title: Recursive expression comparison and its whole-system reduction
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi$, and schemes $W$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On each small pro-etale site set $B_{W,n}=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^n)_W$ for $n\ge1$ and $R_W=\lim_n B_{W,n}$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived category $\mathscr D_W=D(\mathscr S(B_{W,\bullet}))$ of whole semilinear systems, with its tensor and geometric inverse image [lem-coef-semilinear-derived-sections]. A normalized system has invertible transition adjoints $\alpha^A_{m,n}:q_W^*A_m\to A_n$, where $q_W^*=-\otimes^L_{B_{W,m}}B_{W,n}$, for all $m\ge n\ge1$, with the identity and quotient cocycles [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]. For systems $A,N$ on $W$ and $C$ on $Y$, write $T_W(A,N)_n=A_n\otimes^L_{B_{W,n}}N_n$, $F_f(C)_n=Lf_n^*C_n$ for $f:X\to Y$, and $U_W=(B_{W,n}[0])_n$, with the induced whole-system transitions.

Write $\mathcal R_WK=(K\otimes^L_{R_W}B_{W,n})_n$ for coherent reduction [def-weil-integral-reduction-tower] and $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$ for total derived limit of the restricted whole system [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Use the canonical adjunction $\mathcal R_W\dashv\mathcal L_W$ and its natural counit $e_A:\mathcal R_W\mathcal L_WA\to A$ [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], invertible for normalized $A$ [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity]. Let $\widehat T_W,\widehat F_f$ be the actual quotient-complex/Roos completed operations [def-pur-integral-derived-operations].

For finite typed expressions $P$ with input locations and constructors input, coefficient unit, tensor and scheme pullback [def-pur-completed-operation-expressions], let $S_P$ evaluate in $T,F,U$ on normalized inputs, and let $K_P$ evaluate in $\widehat T,\widehat F,\mathcal LU$ on their limits. Define $\beta_P:K_P\to\mathcal L S_P$ recursively by identities at inputs and units, $\beta_{T(P,Q)}=\beta_T(S_P,S_Q)\circ\widehat T(\beta_P,\beta_Q)$ and $\beta_{F_f(P)}=\beta_F(S_P)\circ\widehat F_f(\beta_P)$. Here the primitive maps are those of [lem-pur-completed-primitive-counit-comparison]: the defining quotient realization followed by $\mathcal L T(e_A,e_N)$ and $\mathcal L F_f(e_C)$, respectively. Put $\gamma_P=e_{S_P}\circ\mathcal R(\beta_P)$.

Assume the operations $T,F,U$ preserve normalization and that the two primitive maps just specified are natural isomorphisms on normalized systems. Then for every finite well-typed $P$, $S_P$ is normalized, $\beta_P$ is an isomorphism, and $\gamma_P$ is an isomorphism of whole derived systems. These conclusions hold for the stated recursion, with its given parentheses, including expressions with no input occurrences or with repeated inputs. The induction parameter is the number of operation symbols: both children at a tensor vertex and the child at a pullback vertex are smaller, and inputs and units are the base cases. At each constructor $\beta_P$ is the displayed composite of the functor images of the child comparisons and the specified primitive comparison; the analogous normalization statement uses the closure of $T,F,U$.

For every $m\ge n\ge1$, $\gamma_P$ satisfies the actual transition square
$$\tau^{S_P}_{m,n}(\gamma_P)_m=\operatorname{Res}_{m,n}((\gamma_P)_n)\,\tau^{\mathcal R K_P}_{m,n}.$$
This is the transition equation of the constructed whole-system map $e_{S_P}\mathcal R(\beta_P)$, including $m=n$; equality is not inferred from equality of evaluations. The assertion requires neither faithfulness of finite reduction nor any exchange of tensor and inverse limit. The sets of scheme and input indices may be in independent universes and may be empty; only finite well-typed expressions are evaluated.

proof.text: Use structural induction on the four constructors of [def-pur-completed-operation-expressions], with induction claim that the whole-system value is normalized and the specified recursive beta is invertible, simultaneously over all output locations. This is the finite-expression induction: both tensor children and the pullback child are proper subexpressions, even when the children coincide.

source.place: Agent expansion of extracted original step 7: well-founded induction on finite expression syntax.

proof.text: For an input $i$, $S_i=A_i$ is normalized by the input hypothesis, $K_i=\mathcal L A_i$, and $\beta_i=1_{\mathcal L A_i}$. For a unit at $W$, $S_{1_W}=U_W$ is normalized by the assumed closure for $U$, $K_{1_W}=\mathcal L U_W$, and $\beta_{1_W}=1_{\mathcal L U_W}$. Thus both leaf cases satisfy the claim, with their prescribed identity comparisons.

source.place: Agent expansion of extracted original step 7: input and coefficient-unit base cases.

proof.text: Let $P=T_W(P_1,P_2)$, with both children of output $W$. By induction both $S_{P_j}$ are normalized and $b_j=\beta_{P_j}$ are isomorphisms. The assumed tensor closure makes $S_P=T_W(S_{P_1},S_{P_2})$ normalized. The completed tensor is a bifunctor by [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], so $v=\widehat T_W(b_1,b_2)$ has inverse $\widehat T_W(b_1^{-1},b_2^{-1})$: either composite is the image of the pair of identity maps. Its target is $\widehat T_W(\mathcal L_WS_{P_1},\mathcal L_WS_{P_2})$. Put $c=\beta_T(S_{P_1},S_{P_2})$, the specified quotient realization followed by $\mathcal L_WT_W(e,e)$ in [lem-pur-completed-primitive-counit-comparison]. The primitive-isomorphism hypothesis applies to these normalized children. The prescribed comparison is $\beta_P=c\circ v$, with inverse $v^{-1}\circ c^{-1}$. This proves the tensor induction step without reassociation.

source.place: Agent expansion of extracted original step 7: binary tensor constructor and explicit inverse.

proof.text: Let $P=F_f(Q)$ for $f:X\to Y$, with $Q$ of output $Y$. Induction gives normalized $S_Q$ and an isomorphism $b=\beta_Q:K_Q\to\mathcal L_YS_Q$. The assumed pullback closure makes $S_P=F_f(S_Q)$ normalized. The completed pullback is a functor by [def-pur-integral-derived-operations], so $v=\widehat F_f(b)$ has inverse $\widehat F_f(b^{-1})$, by preservation of composition and identities. Its target is $\widehat F_f(\mathcal L_YS_Q)$. The specified primitive $c=\beta_F(S_Q)$ of [lem-pur-completed-primitive-counit-comparison] is invertible by the hypothesis at this normalized child. Thus the required recursion gives $\beta_P=c\circ v$, with inverse $v^{-1}\circ c^{-1}$. Together with the two leaf cases and the tensor case this proves both induction claims for every finite typed $P$.

source.place: Agent expansion of extracted original step 7: pullback constructor and completion of induction.

proof.text: Fix an expression P. The induction gives normalized systemValue P and invertible beta P. Use the actual whole-system adjunction counit of the supplied reduction record [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. The counit_effective field of the supplied primitive Comparisons record [lem-pur-completed-primitive-counit-comparison], at the identity scheme map, makes this counit invertible on systemValue P. Reduction preserves the beta isomorphism, and their composite, the defined gamma P, is therefore invertible. The normalized-DVR effectivity theorem need not be applied again: its needed consequence is already a hypothesis in Comparisons.

source.place: Agent expansion of extracted original step 8: apply the coherent reduction functor and normalized-system counit.

proof.text: The actual coefficientSequenceDerivedTransition is a natural transformation from evaluation at m to evaluation at n followed by restriction. Apply its naturality equation directly to the constructed whole-system morphism gamma P. This gives exactly the displayed transition square, including m=n. It is equivalent to composing the naturality squares of reduction(beta P) and the actual adjunction counit, and does not infer equality from componentwise evaluations.

source.place: Agent expansion of extracted original step 8: natural transitions for the constructed whole-system composite, with the two factor squares displayed.

proof.text: The constructor cases preserve the given parentheses and only inspect the finitely many vertices of $P$. They never enumerate the available scheme or input sets. With no inputs the unit, tensor and pullback cases alone still apply; if there are no scheme indices there are no output-typed expressions and the assertion is vacuous. Repeated inputs are handled by separate occurrences in the same induction, with no distinctness assumption. Thus arbitrary independent universes for scheme and input indices impose no additional restriction. The proof used the given whole-system maps and functorial inverses throughout, so neither faithfulness of finite reduction nor a tensor/inverse-limit interchange enters the conclusion.
